pitch_detail.notes: 100 ft leading to a large transverse crevasse, crossed on the left.
300 ft through the lower icefall to the headwall base.
Vertical ice in a rock chimney, then 150 ft more steep snow.
60 ft to the glacier tongue.
300 ft of steep ice/snow to the headwall.
100 ft through the headwall weakness to a ledge.
~1,000 ft of good-rock buttress climbing to the SE Ridge crest.
Nisqually/Wilson Glacier crossing below The Castle, exposed to icefall
Steepens gradually
Joins the Fuhrer Finger route on the west side of the Nisqually Glacier
Slabby ice; can be split into two shorter pitches.
Thin, steep ice and mixed ground to the cave entrance.
Traverse right to an overhanging mixed wall to a rock belay.
Snow couloir up to about 55 degrees.
Either continue to the saddle, or take the recommended Post Nasal Drip mixed variation.
Lower icefall step, running belay across the ablation zone/glacier.
Ice ramp between crevasses.
Upper icefall step, extent varies year to year with glacier recession.
Turn right off the ice onto loose rock; scarce protection.
Continued loose rock climbing, running belays typical.
Final rock section to the summit.
Sustained, vertical ice straight up the northwest face.
More moderate ice at roughly 50 degrees.
Steep rime and choss terrain to the summit.
